title: System Explorer collect stream record
description: One NDJSON line of a collect batch (DESIGN 19). A committed collection is authoritative; an uncommitted one is authoritative for nothing. There is no partial commit and no tombstone: everything a committed collection did not emit is gone, and a decline of absent commits empty. Every record type is closed: a member the contract does not name is a claim the judge cannot see (DESIGN 19, two regimes), and an open object is how a Go struct's exported field names shipped as {"Stable":…} without a single test going red.

identity.description: An identity string. Empty is not a name: a join over "" merges everything it touches, and a batch or request of "" makes echo checks vacuously true.

collection_name.description: Mirrors the declaration's collection-name pattern: the stream may only commit under a name a declaration could have declared.

name_scalar.description: A native name is a string or a number, never a structure and never null; minLength binds only the string case.

name_family.description: One stability class's families: each family holds a scalar or a list of scalars — a pool has one guid and several by-id links.

fact_value.description: Any JSON value except null, at any depth: the type list omits null and the array/object branches recurse. The non-recursive rule this replaces refused a null only at the top of the facts dict and passed the same null nested one level down, inside a vdev row — which is exactly where marshalling a struct with nil members puts it.

facts.description: A fact's value is never null, at any depth: could-not-read is the unobservable record and has-no-such-property is the absent list, each on its own channel, and a null names neither (DESIGN 19).

declaration.description: sha256 of the declaration this stream was produced under. Unknown hash: the batch is held un-applied until fetched (DESIGN 25).

boot_id.description: UUID-shaped (8-4-4-4-12 hex) and never the nil UUID — the shape catches the stub and the nil placeholder, which is what a single capture can authenticate; a constant VALID id only varies across boots and is a cross-boot variant's to catch (DESIGN 19). The dashless 32-hex spelling is machine-id's, stable across boots, and refusing it is the point.

timens.description: The collector's CLOCK_BOOTTIME namespace offset. A mismatch with the collator is stated, never corrected (DESIGN 09).

instance.description: Fleet-assigned instance this collector fronts; ids, origins and relations mint under (host, instance) scope. Null means host-native (DESIGN 11, 19) — and only null means it: "" would mint a third scope nobody declared.

generations.description: Collator-issued monotonic generation per collection, echoed. Below-applied commits are refused (DESIGN 19). A fresh acquisition always takes a new generation; retransmission of already-captured output may reuse one.

names.description: Every native name observed for this thing, split by stability class; a join runs on stable only (DESIGN 16, 19). Closed to exactly these two classes: the marshalling bug this catches emitted {"Stable":…,"Ephemeral":…} and every name silently left the join.

absent.description: Declared facts this object genuinely lacks. We looked; there is no such property. Distinct from unobservable (DESIGN 19, 27).

digest.description: Over the redacted payload as served. JSON under the named canon; any other media type over exact post-redaction bytes (DESIGN 19).

evidence.description: JSON digests under a named canonicalisation or the digest is a coin toss over key ordering; any other media type digests exact bytes, so a canon there would claim a rule that was never applied (DESIGN 19).

at.description: CLOCK_BOOTTIME seconds, stamped immediately before the earliest contributing native read, so age never understates (DESIGN 09, 19). Boot-scale by construction: zero and below is a reading nobody took, and past 1e9 (~31 years of uptime) it is a wall clock smuggled onto the wrong axis.

target.description: A name and a kind, never an id, and never an observability: whether the far end was seen is a fact about another collector's output, which only the collator holds (DESIGN 13, 19).

relation_assertion.description: A collector never states observability — whether the far end was seen is a fact about another collector's output, which only the collator holds — and a target carries a name, never an id (DESIGN 13, 19). Both negatives are kept although closure now also refuses them: they encode rulings, not style.

reason.description: The decline vocabulary minus absent: could-not-read-because-it-is-not-there is the absent list's statement, on its own channel (DESIGN 19).

detail.description: Bounded and scrubbed at the collator boundary; this string travels to a hub and out over MCP (DESIGN 19).

decline.description: absent is a successful reading and is followed by a zero-object commit; the other three never commit and mark prior state stale (DESIGN 19).

cpu_ms.description: Measured cost is advisory, never authenticated (DESIGN 19) — but bounded to what a clock can read: non-negative, and JSON itself excludes the non-finite.

commit.description: Always the whole collection: v1 has no partial commit, so a complete member may not appear (DESIGN 19). All three counts are required, never optional — a subject that can disable the truncation check by omitting a count has defeated it.

cpu_ms.description: Bounded like commit.cpu_ms: a cost below zero came off no clock.

wall_ms.description: Bounded like cpu_ms; positivity when objects were emitted is the stream rule, checked where the whole batch is visible.
